# DuckHaven

> DuckHaven is a self-hosted, governed DuckDB + Iceberg analytics platform for small teams.
> It started as collaborative browser worksheets and grew to cover the lifecycle around them:
> an Apache Iceberg catalog governed by Apache Polaris, scheduled queries, an advisory lakehouse
> maintenance scanner, single sign-on, multi-agent DuckDB compute, fine-grained access grants,
> machine auth, and a governed AI data assistant — all on your own infrastructure. It is
> deliberately right-sized (homelab to small team), not an enterprise lakehouse. No cloud
> warehouse lock-in, no Kubernetes, no platform team required.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/installation/): Prerequisites and how to install the stack.
- [Quickstart](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/quickstart/): Stand up the full stack with one `docker compose` command and run your first query.
- [Your first workspace](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/first-workspace/): Create a workspace and invite collaborators.
- [Your first query](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/first-query/): Write and run a query in a browser worksheet.
- [Command line (dh)](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/getting-started/cli-quickstart/): dh is DuckHaven's command-line interface.

## Concepts

- [What is DuckHaven?](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/what-is-duckhaven/): Overview of the product and who it is for.
- [Architecture](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/architecture/): The control-plane / compute split and data flow — the defining idea behind DuckHaven.
- [Workspaces](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/workspaces/): How workspaces isolate queries, permissions, and history.
- [Catalogs & Polaris](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/catalogs/): The shared Iceberg catalog governed by Apache Polaris.
- [Tables & Iceberg](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/tables/): Iceberg-native tables, snapshots, and time travel.
- [Agents](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/agents/): DuckDB compute agents you pick per query.
- [Elastic compute](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/elastic-compute/): By default, agents are static: an operator starts an agent host and it stays running until it is stopped.
- [Storage backends](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/storage-backends/): A storage backend is a physical location where Iceberg table data lives.
- [Query execution](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/query-execution/): Queueing, memory estimation, and concurrency.
- [SQL sessions](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/sql-sessions/): A SQL session is a persistent database connection that DuckHaven holds open on one agent on your behalf, so a client can run many statements with connection-scoped state —…
- [Permissions](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/permissions/): Per-workspace access control and audit trail.
- [AI assistant](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/assistant/): The governed AI data assistant and how it enforces access.
- [MCP server](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/mcp-server/): DuckHaven speaks the Model Context Protocol, so an AI agent running somewhere else — Claude Code in your terminal, Claude Desktop, Cursor — can work with your data directly.
- [Metadata](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/metadata/): DuckHaven splits its state across two stores, and the split is an architectural invariant: catalog structure lives in Polaris, and DuckHaven's own entities live in Postgres.
- [Lineage](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/lineage/): Lineage answers two questions about a table: where did this data come from, and what breaks if I change it.
- [Semantic layer](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/semantic-layer/): A semantic model records what your business terms mean and how they are calculated: that revenue is the sum of amount over purchase events, excluding test accounts, measured on…
- [Lakehouse maintenance](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/concepts/maintenance/): The maintenance advisor is the DuckHaven service that periodically scans every Iceberg table, computes a health score, and raises recommendations for the maintenance each table…

## Deployment

- [Docker Compose](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/install/): Deploy the full stack with Docker Compose.
- [Add an agent](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/add-agent/): Scale compute by adding DuckDB agents.
- [Elastic compute on a single Docker host](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/homelab-elastic-setup/): Enable elastic compute with the Docker backend, provisioning agents as containers on a single host.
- [Elastic compute on Azure](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/azure-elastic-setup/): Enable elastic compute with the Azure Container Instances backend, provisioning agents in the cloud.
- [Configure storage](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/storage/): Point DuckHaven at your object storage backend.
- [Reverse proxy & TLS](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/reverse-proxy-tls/): Front the stack with a reverse proxy and TLS.
- [High availability](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/high-availability/): By default DuckHaven runs a single-node control plane — one Postgres, one Polaris, one API container — which is simple to operate and fine for most installs.
- [Azure with Terraform](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/azure-terraform/): Deploys DuckHaven to Azure as managed infrastructure: the control plane on Container Apps, a managed PostgreSQL server, ADLS Gen2 for Iceberg data, and the plumbing that lets the…
- [Updating](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/updating/): Updates pull a new image and restart the stack.
- [Backup & restore](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/deployment/backup-restore/): Back up and restore DuckHaven data.

## Guides

- [Run queries](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/run-queries/): Day-to-day querying in worksheets.
- [Manage catalogs](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/manage-catalogs/): Create and govern catalogs.
- [Migrate a catalog's storage](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/migrate-catalog-storage/): Move a catalog to a different storage backend without losing data.
- [Snapshots & time travel](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/snapshots-time-travel/): Query tables at a past snapshot.
- [Read query profiles](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/query-profiles/): Inspect operator graphs, timing, and spills.
- [Saved queries](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/saved-queries/): Save a frequently used query so your team can recall and run it later.
- [Schedule queries](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/schedule-queries/): Run a saved query automatically on a schedule — for example "every night at 02:00" — without leaving a worksheet open or wiring up an external cron job.
- [Read the session audit trail](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/session-audit/): When dbt or dlt runs against DuckHaven it opens a SQL session and executes many statements through it.
- [Import lineage from dbt](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/import-dbt-lineage/): If your transformations already live in a dbt project, its DAG is a description of your lineage that somebody has already written down.
- [Define metrics](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/define-metrics/): This guide walks through creating a semantic model, defining a metric, and publishing it so the AI assistant will use it.
- [Import semantics from dbt](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/import-dbt-semantics/): If your metrics are already defined in dbt's semantic layer, DuckHaven can import them rather than making you write them twice.
- [Use the AI assistant](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/using-the-assistant/): Browse the catalog, run SQL, and propose worksheet edits with the assistant.
- [Connect an MCP client](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/connect-mcp-client/): DuckHaven exposes a Model Context Protocol server at /mcp, so an AI agent — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, or anything else that speaks MCP — can browse your catalogs and…
- [How access works](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/access-levels/): The three access layers, including fine-grained catalog/schema/table grants.
- [Manage users & access](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/users-access/): Administer users and permissions.
- [Service accounts & tokens](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/service-accounts/): Machine auth via service accounts and Personal Access Tokens.
- [Connect an IdP (SSO)](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/connect-idp/): DuckHaven can delegate sign-in to one or more OpenID Connect identity providers — Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Authentik, Keycloak, AWS Cognito, Google Workspace, and anything else…
- [Connect LDAP / AD](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/guides/connect-ldap/): As a secondary federated path, DuckHaven can authenticate users against an LDAP directory or Active Directory.

## Operations

- [Operator runbook](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/runbook/): Operational procedures for the single control-plane box plus its agents.
- [Storage security & maintenance](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/storage-maintenance/): Day-2 practice for external S3 and ADLS Gen2 backends: securing access, rotating trust, and routine upkeep.
- [Monitoring](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/monitoring/): DuckHaven gives every agent its own monitoring page, and records a full query audit trail on the History page.
- [Distributed tracing](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/tracing/): DuckHaven emits OpenTelemetry traces alongside the Prometheus metrics.
- [Scaling compute](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/scaling/): DuckHaven scales compute horizontally: the control plane stays small (one box) while you add agents at the edge.
- [HA failover runbook](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/ha-failover/): Drills that prove the highly-available control plane survives the failures it is designed for.
- [Offboarding & break-glass](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/offboarding/): How to remove someone's access cleanly, and how to stay in control when your identity provider is down.
- [Troubleshooting](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/operations/troubleshooting/): Common issues and where to look.

## Reference

- [Configuration](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/configuration/): Every control-plane and agent environment variable.
- [SQL support](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/sql-support/): Supported SQL surface and DuckDB features.
- [Agent reference](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/agent-reference/): Agent configuration and behavior.
- [CLI reference](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/cli/): Every dh command, its summary and its flags.
- [REST API](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/rest-api/): The control-plane REST API.
- [API conventions](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/api-conventions/): The rules every DuckHaven REST endpoint follows.
- [Operator scripts](https://tamasmrtn.github.io/duckhaven/reference/operator-scripts/): DuckHaven ships a few small helper scripts under scripts/ for operators.
